name: Unspecified Mitochondrial Disorder

criteria.description: Presence of multisystem clinical features suggestive of mitochondrial dysfunction
Biochemical demonstration of respiratory chain enzyme deficiency in muscle or other tissues
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial or nuclear DNA variants associated with mitochondrial dysfunction
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-negative fibers
Neuroimaging abnormalities consistent with mitochondrial disease (e.g., basal ganglia lesions)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including clinical features and biochemical evidence, with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, biochemical, histological, and genetic data due to heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of mitochondrial proliferation in muscle fibers
searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Leigh-like basal ganglia lesions on MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic symmetrical lesions in deep brain structures
searchTerms: brain lesions in basal ganglia on MRI

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated lactate levels in blood or CSF
searchTerms: high lactate in blood or spinal fluid

common.notes: Weakness of extraocular muscles leading to ptosis and limited eye movement

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to muscle weakness
common.notes: Reduced capacity for sustained physical activity
searchTerms: fatigue during activity due to muscle weakness
poor exercise tolerance caused by muscle weakness

common.notes: Hearing impairment due to cochlear or neural involvement

occasional.notes: Includes symptoms like constipation and delayed gastric emptying

rare.notes: Transient neurological deficits not explained by vascular occlusion

laboratory: Elevated blood and cerebrospinal fluid lactate and pyruvate
Abnormal respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
Elevated creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Symmetrical basal ganglia and brainstem lesions on MRI
Stroke-like lesions not conforming to vascular territories
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) or nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial function
other: Ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers on muscle histology
Abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant optic neuropathy without multisystem involvement
Typically young adult onset with acute vision loss

redFlags: Progressive multisystem involvement with neurological and muscular symptoms
Elevated lactate in blood or CSF without other explanation
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or respiratory chain defects
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Parikh S, Goldstein A, Karaa A, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015 Sep;17(9):689-701.
